messages:
maya: Quick sync — we need a single metrics/label scheme for runtime + infra dashboards before the rollout next week. cc #eng-runtime and #product. Main concerns: cardinality, which fields to surface in Prom vs OTel, and a migration plan.

sam: +1. rough proposal: keep Prom labels low-card: `service`, `model_family`, `model_variant`, `region`, `env`, `route_normalized`. push high-card stuff (user_id, request_id, prompt_hash) into logs/traces only.

leo: Agree on low-card for Prom. Two calls out: 1) `route` as human path is high-card — we should normalize to a route id. 2) model version/commit -> don't use full hash; use a short `model_tag` (e.g. v1.4, quant-ggml) to avoid explosion.

irene: +1. Also propose a small allowlist for additional labels that product can opt into per-dashboard (max 3 extra labels). Anything else should go into attributes and we can expose via hover/tooltip in the Console.

ashley: Example mapping I used elsewhere: 
```
OTel Resource Attributes -> Prom label
service.name -> service
service.version -> model_tag
deployment.environment -> env
cloud.region -> region
custom.runtime.route_id -> route_normalized
custom.runtime.model_family -> model_family
```
Note: avoid `user.id`, `request.id`, `session.id` as Prom labels.

maya: That mapping looks good. Thoughts on cardinality thresholds? We should set a guideline like "labels with >1000 unique values/month -> banned" and have the telemetry team run an audit.

sam: We can add a CI check that scans upcoming metric definitions and flags any label whose cardinality estimate > 1k. We already have a small script in infra-monitoring that uses sample logs to estimate unique counts. I'll prototype.

leo: Also need to decide how to handle rollouts: when a model is canaried, we still want separate metrics for the canary variant. So `model_tag` must include the canary name but be controlled (short strings).

irene: For dashboards, recommend base set: request_rate, p50/p95/p99 latency, token_count, error_rate, cost_per_token. All with labels: service, model_family, model_tag, region, env, route_normalized. Additional per-team panels can include the 3 allowlisted labels.

ashley: Small Prom snippet for metric naming and labels: 
```
# HELP runtime_request_duration_seconds request latency
# TYPE runtime_request_duration_seconds histogram
runtime_request_duration_seconds_bucket{service="runtime",model_family="gptx",model_tag="v1.4",env="prod",region="us-west-2",route_normalized="r_345"} 123
```
Keep metric names kebab/case consistent: `runtime_*` for runtime, `infra_*` for infra platform.

ops-bot: telemetry-audit: found 12 existing metrics with >500 unique `route` values across last 30d. Recommend migration plan and gradual rollouts.

maya: Good catch. Proposed migration plan: (1) create `route_normalized` attribute and backfill mapping for existing `route` values for top 200 routes; (2) run audit and add CI guardrails; (3) update dashboards to rely on normalized label; (4) deprecate raw `route` label after 30 days. Can we get owners?

sam: I'll take the CI guard (prototype this week).

leo: Eng-runtime will own backfill mapping; we can start with top 200 and then automate via a normalization service.

irene: Product/console will update dashboards — I'll coordinate the allowlist per team.

maya: Great. Action items: sam -> CI/scan, leo -> backfill plan, irene -> dashboard changes, ashley -> write PR with mapping docs. I'll open a short RFC and link it here. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:

ashley: FYI I'll include the OTel<->Prom mapping table and a short set of DOs/DON'Ts in the RFC to reduce bikeshedding.

maya: RFC here: https://rwd.internal/rfcs/metrics-schema-2026 (temporary link)

ops-bot: deploy-bot: created task #1234 "metrics-schema: add cardinality CI check" assigned to sam.
